task: Rebuild the project website from the approved mockup: Slate palette, skills-first home, install page, councils shown read-only

independent.stance: Follow the mockup closely; its calm, rounded layout fixes the noise problem.
keyArguments: The approved mockup replaces six competing accent colours with one accent and one secondary voice (VERIFIED_FACT: mockup source, Council Downloads.dc.html).
A skills-first home page answers the first question a visitor has: what do I get and how do I install it.
risks: Mockup copy uses placeholder names and package commands that do not exist for this project.
assumptions: Visitors are developers evaluating whether to install (ASSUMPTION).

independent.stance: Build it, but do not copy anything the project cannot back up.
keyArguments: The mockup shows 'claude plugins install', an npm package, a 48-skill count and an 18 MB zip. None of these exist here (VERIFIED_FACT: package is not on npm, see installer/cli.js help text).
Download buttons must not appear unless a real file can be served.
risks: Shipping invented install commands would break the anti-slop baseline (BL-002, BL-003).
assumptions: The local web server is how most people view the site (ASSUMPTION).

independent.stance: Five top-level destinations named by what people do.
keyArguments: The old header exposed six system-named areas plus a status ribbon (VERIFIED_FACT: web/index.html before this change).
Skills, Councils, Agents, Gates and Install map to the questions visitors actually ask.
risks: Moving the code reviewer into Gates may make it harder to find.
assumptions: The council page is read-only; sessions are run from the agent, not the browser (VERIFIED_FACT: user decision, 2026-10-08).

independent.stance: Adopt the mockup but keep text contrast at AA and add real semantics.
keyArguments: The design system notes the accent-on-ground pair is tuned to 3:1, enough for large text and chrome but not body text (VERIFIED_FACT: _ds readme, Interaction states).
The old app had no ARIA roles or focus styles (VERIFIED_FACT: discovery audit).
risks: Muted text at 55% opacity can fall below 4.5:1 on the surface colour.
assumptions: Most visitors use a pointer, but keyboard paths must still work (ASSUMPTION).

independent.stance: Use the Slate palette as generated, with ramp steps instead of ad-hoc mixes.
keyArguments: Slate is generated in OKLCH from one lightness scale, so tints and text steps stay even (VERIFIED_FACT: mockup paletteCss function).
One violet accent plus a muted teal second voice is enough; status colours stay separate.
risks: Low-chroma neutrals can look grey and flat at large sizes.
assumptions: The user prefers a neutral palette over the warm Organic default (VERIFIED_FACT: user chose Slate, 2026-10-08).
evidence: Mockup PALETTES.Slate: bg hue 260, accent [275, .18], second [200, .08]

challenges.critique: 'Follow the mockup closely' would ship its placeholder install commands, counts and file sizes.
challenges.counterProposal: Keep the layout; replace every command, count and size with values read from the repository at build time.

challenges.critique: Five destinations plus search plus a code checker is still a lot for a first release.
challenges.counterProposal: Keep the code checker as one section inside Gates rather than its own page.

challenges.critique: Accent text on the light ground is only tuned for 3:1.
challenges.counterProposal: Use the 700 accent step for links and small accent text; reserve the base accent for fills and large type.

challenges.critique: Hiding all download buttons loses a useful part of the mockup.
challenges.counterProposal: Show Download ZIP only when the local server confirms it can build the archive with git archive.

whatChanged: All commands, counts and sizes come from repository data, not the mockup.
whatRemainedUnchanged: Layout, type and shapes follow the mockup.

responses.reason: Placeholder values would be false claims.

whatRemainedUnchanged: Would ship to the local site first and review real use before publishing it anywhere public.

responses.reason: Fine when the server can produce the file; the button must not appear otherwise.

whatChanged: Code checker moves into the Gates page as a section.
whatRemainedUnchanged: Five destinations: Skills, Councils, Agents, Gates, Install.

responses.reason: It belongs with quality gates anyway.

whatRemainedUnchanged: AA contrast for body text; visible focus on every control.

whatChanged: Links and small accent text use accent-700.

responses.reason: The 700 step keeps the hue and clears 4.5:1.

brief.topic: Rebuild the project website from the approved mockup: Slate palette, skills-first home, install page, councils shown read-only
strongestArgumentsFor: The mockup removes the visual noise found in the discovery audit.
A skills-first home and a plain install page answer what visitors need first.
strongestArgumentsAgainst: The mockup's commands and numbers are placeholders that do not exist for this project.

evidence.statement: The package is not published to npm.
The Slate palette is generated in OKLCH with accent hue 275.
Most visitors are developers deciding whether to install.

assumptions: Visitors are developers evaluating the framework.
The site is mostly viewed through the local server.
unknowns: Whether the repository will become public, which would allow hosted downloads.

tradeOffs.chosen: ZIPs built locally with git archive

risks.description: Data drift if the site stops reading from repository files

mitigations: Build all counts and commands from repository data in web/build-data.js.
Contrast tests for text tokens in the validation suite.
mvpScope: Skills, Councils, Agents, Gates and Install pages
Slate tokens with the Organic type and shapes

validationExperiments.hypothesis: Visitors can install without reading the README
validationExperiments.experiment: Ask two developers to install from the Install page alone

successMetrics.target: Every text token at or above 4.5:1 on its surface

conditionsToChange: The repository becomes public, allowing hosted downloads and a real one-line installer.

dissent.rationale: Would ship to the local site first and review real use before publishing it anywhere public.
